Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg on what he’s learned playing with Steph Curry:

“Honestly, besides all the movement, moving stuff that he does, now that I’m watching it firsthand, like he’s really getting grabbed and held every single play, like no freedom of movement. And it’s like, I think that’s kind of why he has to run away. Like he’s essentially getting away. Like he’s being chased around all day. So I mean, that’s where all that stamina comes from and all those practice reps of him just running around screens and looking crazy. But it’s like, it’s really needed for him to be able to get the ball, get open looks. I mean, that’s something I’ve understood right away. And then just his, like, routine, because I know a lot of people say he’s a superstitious guy, but I mean, that kind of stuff really plays a big part in, like, the mental side of the basketball game.”

On their developing two-man chemistry:

“Absolutely. He’s definitely been talking to me a lot about, you know, just having those opportunities to create those mismatches. You know, there’s a lot of people that are going to, you know, go towards him. Whenever he’s setting a ball screen or a back screen, it’s going to leave me with wide open looks. We’ve seen that against the Kings. We’ve seen that against the Lakers. You know, it was different opportunities in different times where I got myself open because of his back screen. You know, so I feel like it’s going to be very easy to find some kind of two-man game with Steph and just being able to play off him.”

NFLPA statement on @JalenHurts: “The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.”
Sills is impassioned on this topic—"The sacred trust we as physicians have with our patients is very, very special to us."

NFL EVP Troy Vincent says 40% of starters league-wide didn't play in the preseason, and that he believes it contributes to the early-season uptick in penalties, and sloppy quality of play. "I truly believe to be a good tackler, you have to tackle, and not just in practice."

NFL's Dr. Allen Sills: "I will say this, I have tremendous confidence in the Eagles medical staff, and all our medical staffs ... Our first obligation is always, and evermore will be, to the patient. ... There is no doctor who is taking orders from a football person."

One other detail on the Jalen Hurts situation: The @Eagles quarterback was treated at the Cleveland Clinic in London. That arrangement is done for international games by NFL medical czar Dr. Allen Sills, who works on it with his counterpart from the Premier League.

NFL's Peter O'Reilly says the league is considering going to 10 international games, which is the CBA limit, in 2027. He said he doesn't know yet if the NFL will go to a new country next year, but did reference the idea of going to new cities in countries they've been to.

NFL’s Peter O’Reilly: “All our plans for the Paris game are moving forward.” Says the league has had people on the ground in Paris for 10 days.
